title: finding(core): `Registry.registerLazy` takes the same bare-name fallback branch as `register` with NO collision check, while `register` warns — measured as zero warnings while two declarations contested one bare key
body:
Measured by the `os-dev` lane executing objectui#9533's maintainer ruling, and **re-verified by the reviewing seat** — the asymmetry is confirmed at both call sites by block, not by grep.

## What

`packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts` has two registration doors, and both take the same bare-name fallback branch. Only one of them checks for a collision.

| door | opens at | `meta?.namespace && !meta?.skipFallback` branch | collision warning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `register` | `:457` | ✅ present (`:492`) | ✅ present (`:501`) — *"Component \"…\" bare-name fallback is being overwritten by \"…\". … pass `{ skipFallback: true }` so it doesn't claim the bare \"…\" key."* |
| `registerLazy` | `:556` | ✅ present | ⛔ **absent** |

⇒ a lazy registration can take the bare key away from another declaration and say nothing at all.

## ⭐ Measured, not inferred — and the measurement is a by-product of a live defect

objectui#9533's own reproduction, run against a real `Registry` before any fix existed, emitted **zero** collision warnings **while two declarations were contesting the bare `dashboard` key**. ⇒ the silence is a reading, not an absence of evidence.

⭐ And that is precisely why that defect survived to be filed at all: **two of its three claimants were `registerLazy` calls.** The shape came in through the door with no check. That is not a coincidence — it is the mechanism by which this class stays invisible.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a two-line patch

⚠️ Adding the warning is mechanically small and the question underneath is not:

- `registerLazy` runs at **stub** time, before the module loads, so at that moment the registry may legitimately hold a bare entry the lazy one is about to replace with its own real registration. A warning keyed the same way `register` keys its own may fire on the ordinary, correct sequence.
- ⇒ deciding **when** a lazy bare-key claim is a collision and when it is the normal lifecycle is the card's actual content. ⛔ Not decided here.

⚠️ And a second-order effect worth pricing before anyone acts: objectui#9264's gate and its shrink-only ledger read the *declared* population. A new warning changes what is noisy at runtime, ⛔ not what that ledger holds; the two should not be conflated.

## Not measured

⛔ How many first-party `registerLazy` calls take the fallback branch today, and how many of those would newly warn — no census was run. ⛔ Whether any first-party sequence relies on the silence. ⛔ Whether `register`'s own warning text is right for the lazy case; it names `skipFallback` as the remedy, which may or may not be the right advice before a module has loaded.

Refs: objectui#9533 (the ruling whose reproduction measured the silence; two of its three claimants were `registerLazy`) · objectui#6416 (the earlier convergence off this shape) · objectui#9264 (the gate and shrink-only ledger that read the declared population).
